Chief Wole Olanipekun, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria, has revealed that President Bola Tinubu expressed his ambition to govern Nigeria as far back as 1992, during the inauguration of the National Assembly under the military regime of General Ibrahim Babangida. Olanipekun said Tinubu, who was then a senator, addressed his colleagues at the gathering and told Babangida that members of the National Assembly had an interest in the survival of democracy because some of them hoped to govern the country in the future. The senior lawyer made the revelation on Thursday at the presentation of his six-volume book, Wole Olanipekun Through the Cases, which documents cases handled by his law firm, Wole Olanipekun & Co. The event, held at the Body of Benchers Complex in Abuja, also marked his 75th birthday, 50 years at the Nigerian Bar and 35 years as a Senior Advocate of Nigeria. Tinubu attended the ceremony, unveiled the publication and conferred the Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger on him. Olanipekun spoke while recounting his longstanding relationship with Tinubu, dating back to 1992, when he was the Attorney-General of the old Ondo State. According to him, Tinubu’s remarks at the National Assembly inauguration made a lasting impression on him, particularly his declaration that some of the senators aspired to lead the country. He said the President’s emergence as Nigeria’s leader in 2023 was a fulfilment of the ambition he had expressed more than three decades earlier. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. You told President Babangida that you, every one of us in this country, particularly you senators, had an insurable interest in democracy because one day people like you wanted to govern this country. That was 1992. “As God will have it, in 2023, you became President of Nigeria. And here you are, seated today as the President of Nigeria. You never knew then, but it is said, it is written, after the abundance of the heart, the mouth speaketh. “You said it; it came to pass. We started. It was then I got attracted to you, Your Excellency.” The lawyer also recalled Tinubu’s involvement in efforts to challenge the dissolution of the National Assembly following the 1993 military coup led by the late General Sani Abacha. He said Tinubu, alongside some other senators, approached him and his senior colleague, the late G.O.K. Ajayi, SAN, at a meeting held at the residence of the late Senator Odi Adewumi on Agoro Doyin Street. Tinubu asked me to challenge governor’s impeachment – Olanipekun Tinubu confers GCON on Olanipekun Olanipekun @75: The man, his mission and milestone According to Olanipekun, the politicians briefed them to challenge the dissolution of the legislature in court. He said, “At that nocturnal meeting at Agoro Doyin Street, in the residence of late Senator Odi Adewumi, you briefed my boss, one of my bosses in the profession, G.O.K. Ajayi, and myself that we should challenge the dissolution. “We did file an action, but later withdrew it for exigencies of that time. Shortly thereafter, we didn’t see you because we couldn’t locate our clients and couldn’t be fighting any cause on behalf of a client that we don’t see, because you had disappeared. You had to travel; you had to leave.” Olanipekun said Tinubu later returned and assigned him and other lawyers to work with senior lawyer Chi Williams on his legal matters. He described the President as someone who appreciated the contributions of lawyers, recalling that Tinubu wrote him a letter in July 2003 after the conclusion of a legal case involving Mitchell Williams and Tinubu. He said the letter contained commendations that humbled him and would be included in his memoirs. “I’m not doing any campaign, but I’m talking as a lawyer. I’m talking of what I’ve seen. “I’m not talking of what I’ve witnessed or what I’ve experienced. At first hand, I did not only work for you, Mr President, but you’ve always appreciated lawyers. This is very important to our profession,” he said. The senior lawyer said the letter was particularly meaningful to him because it reflected Tinubu’s appreciation of his professional contribution. “You wrote me a letter in July 2003. That letter definitely will go into my memoirs. You said a lot about me. “I was humbled. That was when we completed the case of Mitchell Williams and Tinubu. It’s in one of these volumes,” he added. Olanipekun said his experiences working with Tinubu and other political figures reinforced the importance of defending democracy and the rule of law. He said the accounts, alongside other legal engagements handled by his firm, were documented in the six-volume publication unveiled at the event.
